raw: {"questions": [{"question": "Which protocol uses a three-way handshake involving SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK?", "options": {"A": "UDP", "B": "IP", "C": "TCP", "D": "FTP"}, "answer": "C", "explanation": "TCP is connection-oriented and sets up a connection using a three-way handshake."}, {"question": "What is the minimum header size of a TCP segment?", "options": {"A": "8 bytes", "B": "20 bytes", "C": "32 bytes", "D": "64 bytes"}, "answer": "B", "explanation": "TCP has a minimum 20-byte header, compared to UDP's small 8-byte header."}, {"question": "Which of the following applications uses UDP instead of TCP according to the notes?", "options": {"A": "HTTP", "B": "Email (SMTP)", "C": "File transfer (FTP)", "D": "DNS queries"}, "answer": "D", "explanation": "DNS queries use UDP because speed matters more than perfect reliability."}, {"question": "How does TCP guarantee reliable, in-order delivery?", "options": {"A": "Using sequence numbers, acknowledgements and retransmission", "B": "Using a connectionless handshake and flow control", "C": "Using an 8-byte header and low latency", "D": "Using congestion control and no acknowledgements"}, "answer": "A", "explanation": "TCP guarantees reliable, in-order delivery using sequence numbers, acknowledgements, and retransmission."}, {"question": "Why is UDP faster and lower in latency than TCP?", "options": {"A": "It uses a three-way handshake", "B": "It is connectionless with no handshake and a smaller header", "C": "It guarantees delivery and order using a sliding window", "D": "It uses congestion control for email and file transfers"}, "answer": "B", "explanation": "UDP is connectionless, lacks a handshake, has no delivery guarantees, and features a smaller 8-byte header."}]}

questions.question: Which protocol uses a three-way handshake involving SYN, SYN-ACK, and ACK?
questions.explanation: TCP is connection-oriented and sets up a connection using a three-way handshake.

questions.question: What is the minimum header size of a TCP segment?
questions.explanation: TCP has a minimum 20-byte header, compared to UDP's small 8-byte header.

questions.question: Which of the following applications uses UDP instead of TCP according to the notes?
questions.explanation: DNS queries use UDP because speed matters more than perfect reliability.

questions.question: How does TCP guarantee reliable, in-order delivery?

options.A: Using sequence numbers, acknowledgements and retransmission
options.B: Using a connectionless handshake and flow control
options.C: Using an 8-byte header and low latency
options.D: Using congestion control and no acknowledgements

questions.explanation: TCP guarantees reliable, in-order delivery using sequence numbers, acknowledgements, and retransmission.

questions.question: Why is UDP faster and lower in latency than TCP?

options.B: It is connectionless with no handshake and a smaller header
options.C: It guarantees delivery and order using a sliding window
options.D: It uses congestion control for email and file transfers

questions.explanation: UDP is connectionless, lacks a handshake, has no delivery guarantees, and features a smaller 8-byte header.
